html:
A famine in Ireland from 1845 to 1852, caused by potato blight. About a million people died of hunger and disease, and about a million more emigrated.

Ireland was then part of the United Kingdom. Since the potato spread in Europe, it had become almost the only food of Ireland's rural poor, who rented tiny plots from mostly absentee landlords. In 1845 a mould, Phytophthora infestans, probably from the Americas, rotted the crop. It failed again in the following years.

The British government's response was slow and shaped by belief in free markets. Some relief was given, including soup kitchens and public works, and Prime Minister Robert Peel repealed the Corn Laws. But food continued to be exported from Ireland, and many tenants were evicted.

Ireland's population fell by about a quarter, and it kept falling for decades through emigration. Millions went to the United States, Britain, Canada and Australia, creating a large Irish diaspora. The famine left deep bitterness toward British rule and fed the movement for Irish independence.
sum: A famine in Ireland from 1845 to 1852, caused by potato blight. About a million people died of hunger and disease, and about a million more emigrated.
